content_preview.title: Bun 1.4.4 Adds bun fmt, a Built-In Prettier-Compatible Formatter That Bun Says Runs 286x Faster Than Prettier on Prettier's Own Repository
content_preview.summary: Bun's v1.4.4 release adds a built-in code formatter, bun fmt; Bun's own benchmark lists 59.7 ms against 17.1 s for Prettier on Prettier's repository.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Bun v1.4.4 introduces `bun fmt`, a formatter built into the runtime. According to the [Bun blog post for v1.4.4](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4.4), written by Jarred Sumner and dated October 22, 2026, "bun fmt is an incredibly fast, Prettier-compatible code formatter that works with your existing Prettier or oxfmt config." The release is also listed on [GitHub](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/bun-v1.4.4) as Bun v1.4.4. All performance and compatibility figures below are B...

editor_notes.content_quality: Compact, well-structured Briefing (563 words, range 300-800). Overview, What We Know, What We Don't Know and Other Changes sections are clear. Vendor figures are consistently labelled as Bun's own and not independently reproduced. The title attributes the 286x headline to 'Bun Says'.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read source-0.html.gz (bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4.4, HTTP 200, snapshot sha256 e9af8ca2...) via raw HTML text extraction, plus a live re-fetch with curl (page bytes differ from the snapshot, as expected for a dynamic page; every key string re-confirmed live: '286x faster', '3x to 6x faster than oxfmt 0.74.0', '234x to 425x faster than Prettier 3.9.9', '9,731', '1,343', 'exits with code 2'). Verified individually against the post: byline Jarred Sumner and date October 22, 2026; verbatim quote 'bun fmt is an incredibly fast, Prettier-compatible code formatter that works with your existing Prettier or oxfmt config'; language list (JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, Flow, CSS, SCSS, Less, HTML, Vue, Svelte, Angular, Lightning Web Components, MJML, JSON, JSONC, JSON5, YAML, TOML, Markdown, MDX, GraphQL, Handlebars) and embedded code; Prettier's own repo 2,616 files with their config, bun fmt --check 59.7 ms / 48 MB vs Prettier 3.9.10 17.1 s / 459 MB, 'That's 286x faster' (the post's prose rounds to 60 ms and 17 seconds; the table gives the article's precise figures); vitest, date-fns, monkeytype, h3 '234x to 425x faster than Prettier 3.9.9' (verbatim); oxfmt '3x to 6x faster than oxfmt 0.74.0' (verbatim), table RSSHub/redocly-cli/vite/fumadocs with fumadocs 31x; one-core table 1.7x (redocly-cli) to 21x (fumadocs); hardware 16-core M4 Max MacBook Pro for vite (mean) and Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C for the rest (median); config files read (.prettierrc*, prettier.config.*, 'prettier' key in package.json, .editorconfig, .prettierignore, .oxfmtrc.json/.jsonc, oxfmt.config.ts/.mts); --check, --staged, --changed; built-in import sorting; unsupported plugin such as prettier-plugin-jsdoc prints an error naming the plugin, skips affected files, exits code 2; lineage quote 'It's a port of Prettier, and the JavaScript and TypeScript printer is a port of oxc_formatter, which is a port of Biome's formatter' (verbatim) and thanks to the Prettier, Biome and Oxc teams; compatibility: CI runs Prettier 3.9.9's own formatting tests on every commit, 9,731 tests / 9,648 identical / 99.1% (defined as byte-for-byte identical output), oxfmt 0.72 on 1,343 of 1,498 fixtures (89.7%); intentional difference: Prettier 3.9.9 drops <!DOCTYPE html> in Handlebars, bun fmt keeps it; bun check '1.4x to 7.8x faster on large projects' (verbatim), MUI docs 10.28 s to 1.31 s, peak memory 11.2 GB to 1.3 GB; bun install converts Yarn 2+ (Berry) yarn.lock to bun.lock; retries up to five times, 50 ms first delay, doubling. All confirmed. The 'built into Bun' and 'Prettier-compatible' wording follows the post exactly (a bun fmt command; not described as opt-in or gated). The post's 330-repository comparison is not used by the article, so nothing depends on it. Read source-1.html.gz (GitHub release page, HTTP 200): title 'Bun v1.4.4', tag bun-v1.4.4; cited only to show the release exists, which it does. GitHub API: published_at 2026-10-22T10:11:32Z, not draft, not prerelease, confirming October 22, 2026. Internal link /article/2026-10/10-bun-143-adds-bun-check-... resolves to the published Bun 1.4.3 article and is described accurately (bun check type checker). suspicious_patterns: null for both sources. Allowlist: github.com (line 1131) and bun.com (line 2387, already listed with a first-party justification comment) both match by exact hostname; no allowlist change needed. Orphan-link diff: every URL in the body (bun.com blog, GitHub release) is in article.sources; only other link is the internal Herald path. Single-vendor sourcing for all performance and compatibility claims: no independent coverage cited; the article says so explicitly. Independent-source count not applicable (Briefing).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No discrepancies found. Minor imprecision: the article calls the second table 'restricted to one core', but that table also contains a vite row (1,608 files, 3.6x) not marked one-core; the stated 1.7x to 21x range is unaffected because the one-core rows give 1.7x, 1.9x and 21x. Too small for a correction. Hardware attribution (M4 Max for vite, Xeon for the rest) matches the post's footnote.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and strictly attributive. Every benchmark and compatibility figure is introduced as the Bun blog's or Bun's own claim; no endorsement or evaluative language; no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: New release not previously covered. The earlier Bun 1.4.3 article (bun check) is a different release and is linked appropriately; the bun check improvements mentioned here are new in 1.4.4 and sourced to the 1.4.4 post. Related archive pieces (Bun 1.4 stable, Bun Zig-to-Rust rewrite) are not duplicates.
concerns: CONFLICT OF INTEREST (verified): Bun is owned by Anthropic. The Herald archive documents this: the 2026-04 Bun 1.1.13 article states Bun was 'acquired by Anthropic in December 2025' and cites The Register and InfoQ; the 2026-05 article on the Zig-to-Rust rewrite states the company 'acquired the project in December 2025', that Bun is 'a project Anthropic owns', and that the Rust port was by Sumner's own account produced by Anthropic's Claude; the 2026-08 Bun 1.4 article repeats that Sumner used Claude for the port. The cited Bun blog page itself carries the footer 'Now part of Anthropic' and '© 2026 Anthropic, PBC'. Anthropic makes the model family that powers this newsroom's writer and reviewer. The article under review does not mention Anthropic, makes no evaluative claim, and attributes every performance and compatibility figure to Bun, so it remains strictly attributive; the relationship is disclosed here in the editorial record. No correction required.
All performance and compatibility figures come from one vendor source and were not independently reproduced; the article states this.
recommendations: Future Bun coverage could mention the Anthropic ownership in the body where the vendor's own benchmarks are the lead.
Describe the one-core table precisely (it also contains a non-one-core vite row).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, properly attributed Briefing; every checked specific traces to the cited Bun blog post and the release exists on GitHub. Verdict APPROVE. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate vendor-sourced release coverage of a built-in formatter for a defined JavaScript developer audience, with benchmarks that are single-vendor claims
